reviews.project_title: from unexpected from to design possibility
reviews.contribution: This project proposes an intermediate, practice-based framework that explains how AI-generated semantic deviations can trigger abductive reasoning, meaning reconstruction, and reflective design decisions in human–AI co-creation, demonstrated through six parametrically generated 3D-printed objects.
reviews.strongest_support: Each of the six objects retains its parameters, dimensions, and formal evolution, allowing deviations to be traced rather than treated as random errors. These records connect specific asymmetric rules and semantic ruptures to the designer’s subsequent reinterpretation and design decisions.
reviews.main_challenge: The claim that semantic deviation triggers abductive reasoning currently relies mainly on the designer’s own interpretation and lacks independent evidence. It could be strengthened through a systematic comparison of the six objects, a documented reflective protocol, and feedback from external designers or researchers.

reviews.project_title: a wall-scale pond of light, generated live from a checked eDNA corpus — the case, not the contribution
reviews.contribution: The project contributes a three-layer framework—negotiated legibility, four rights of withholding, and evidence-graded provenance—for designing interfaces that communicate uncertainty without inventing biological presence. The wall-scale pond of light generated from a verified eDNA corpus is the case through which this framework is tested, not the contribution itself.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the necessity test: without constructing the pond, the project cannot demonstrate that an evidential limit can function simultaneously as a machine state and a public interface. Its five controls alter the visual environment while exposing how each interaction spends a different form of certainty.
reviews.main_challenge: The principle of withholding still depends on the designer deciding what evidence viewers are allowed to access. The argument would be strengthened by documented viewer walk-throughs and failure-mode analysis showing when each restriction clarifies uncertainty, becomes confusing, or reinforces excessive designer authority.

reviews.project_title: SIX SHEETS.ONLY THE LINE WEIGHT CHANGES
reviews.contribution: The project contributes an annotated-portfolio method for identifying the physical threshold at which geometrically distinct signs become visually indistinguishable through changes in line weight. The six sheets make visible how material production conditions can determine whether a geometric alphabet continues to function as a language.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the controlled comparison across six sheets: the geometric rule remains unchanged, while only the line weight varies. This isolates the moment when lines that remain separate on screen merge after physical production, making the machine’s minimum printable gap observable.
reviews.main_challenge: The proposed threshold may vary according to the machine, material, production settings, and viewing distance, while the physical tests have not yet been completed. The claim would be strengthened through calibrated fabrication, repeated trials, and an independent recognition test showing when viewers can no longer distinguish the signs.

reviews.project_title: TraceWithin
reviews.contribution: The project contributes a research-through-design method for examining how the duration of visible breath traces and the gradual withdrawal of guidance jointly influence independent mindfulness practice. Its contribution is the temporal feedback mechanism and matched comparison protocol, rather than the VR experience itself.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the matched 2 × 2 comparison of immediate versus persistent feedback and continuous versus withdrawn guidance, followed by the same task without feedback. This design directly tests whether support improves independent practice or instead increases workload and technological dependence.
reviews.main_challenge: The proposed contribution currently lacks empirical evidence because the prototype and pilot study have not yet been completed. It would be strengthened by preregistered outcome criteria, reliable respiratory recordings, validated attention measures, and a common transfer test conducted both inside and outside VR.

reviews.project_title: "memories"of the sea
reviews.contribution: This project contributes an analytical framework explaining how textual content, attribution, material form, spatial arrangement, and public participation collectively establish commemorated subjects and produce—or fail to produce—monumentality. The Macau street-name installation is a design case used to test this framework, rather than being the contribution itself.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the comparative analysis of Jenny Holzer’s VIGIL and Doris Salcedo’s Quebrantos, which examines concrete differences in naming, attribution, authorization, and public action. Applying the same analytical dimensions to the Macau prototype creates a clear connection between theoretical analysis and design practice.
reviews.main_challenge: The main unsupported claim is that temporariness, visibility, and participation can collectively generate monumentality, because there is not yet enough evidence of how audiences interpret the installation. The project could be strengthened through consistent cross-case criteria and public evaluation methods, such as observation, interviews, or documented participant responses.

reviews.project_title: beyond patterns:the hidden bodily knowledge in lantian dai-zai weaving
reviews.contribution: This project contributes a three-step field method for identifying the tacit bodily judgements—such as tension, tightness, and humidity—that conventional video archives fail to capture. Its annotated woven samples also provide a practical reference for future heritage documentation and digital translation.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence is the comparison between the master and novice, showing that copying visible hand movements reproduced only 60% of the original weaving density. Recording errors, reworking processes, and “feel”-based explanations convincingly reveals the hidden judgements behind the craft.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is demonstrating that the proposed method can reliably identify tacit knowledge rather than merely collect subjective interview accounts. Testing it with more weavers, materials, and weaving contexts would strengthen its validity and wider applicability.

reviews.project_title: From AI-Generated Parts to Physical Sculpture: Selection, Rejection, and Assembly in Human–AI Co-Creation
reviews.contribution: This project shows how human creativity emerges after AI generation through the selection, rejection, physical interlocking, and composition of generated parts. It contributes a materially grounded account of human agency in transforming disconnected AI outputs into a coherent sculpture.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the completed 3D-printed sculpture together with documented records of rejected components, selection decisions, and assembly iterations. This evidence makes the human contribution traceable rather than treating the final artifact alone as proof.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is distinguishing meaningful creative judgement from ordinary curation or practical problem-solving. The project needs explicit criteria for analysing why components were selected or rejected and how those decisions shaped the sculpture’s visual rhythm, movement, and coherence.

reviews.project_title: Parametric Decoding in History: Correspondences between Geometric Shapes and Historical Sites in the 1889 Praia Grande
reviews.contribution: This project contributes an evidence-based parametric coding method that translates five historical variables—weight, scale, radius, defence, and decay—into coordinate-registered 3D geometry. By overlaying this geometry with the 1889 fabric map, it makes the visual gap between documentary authority and historical erasure the central argument.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the direct alignment of the documentary map and the white 3D geometry on the same geographical coordinates. The traceable connection between historical evidence, coding rules, and material output allows the object itself to function as an argument rather than mere visualization.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is proving that the five parameters are historically justified rather than subjective formal interpretations. The project therefore needs verified sources and transparent coding rules explaining how each historical condition is translated into a specific geometric property.

reviews.project_title: idal Rhythm: A Five-State Generative Lightbox
reviews.contribution: This project contributes a reproducible five-state method—rising, slowing, ebb, still, and returning tide—for introducing planned rest into continuously running generative light installations. It translates the abstract idea of visual rest into controllable changes in motion, speed, and visual density.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the full-cycle physical prototype combining a 3D-printed shell, diffuser, programmable RGB LEDs, and visible state transitions. This enables the relationship between timing, light diffusion, and perceived movement to be evaluated directly.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is demonstrating that five states create a more meaningful experience of rest than a simple active/rest switch. A comparative test and audience feedback would help define whether viewers can perceive each state and experience the intended tidal rhythm.

reviews.project_title: Living Data Forest: Inhabiting More-than-Human Data
reviews.contribution: This project contributes an enterable and playable “data forest” that transforms weather, bird, and species data from screen-based charts into evolving spatial forms. It also creates a circular data ecology in which visitors’ traces and sightings return to shape the forest.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the complete pipeline connecting open data, nonhuman flocking algorithms, daily evolving forms, visitor participation, and printable objects. The use of site-specific data, including Cotai’s tides and spoonbill sightings, prevents the project from becoming a generic data-visualization tool.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is demonstrating that entering and interacting with the forest genuinely creates kinship with more-than-human beings. Comparative user evaluation is needed to show whether the embodied experience produces deeper understanding than conventional charts while avoiding claims that the system speaks for other species.

reviews.project_title: Forest: AI Reinvented Nature
reviews.contribution: This project contributes a comparative method for examining how authored mappings and independent AI interpretations of the same human behaviour generate different ecological responses. Its annotated portfolio makes interpretation visible as a design decision and develops practical knowledge for human–artificial-environment relationships.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the controlled A/B comparison in which both systems receive the same observable behaviour and operate under identical ecological rules. Annotated visual evidence can clearly trace how different interpretations lead to different environmental consequences.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is defining and measuring “ecological response” clearly enough for the comparison to be reproducible. The project should specify the fixed rules, AI decision boundaries, and evaluation criteria, while explaining why the forest setting is necessary rather than merely illustrative.

reviews.project_title: Neural Landscape: Live EEG as Artistic Material
reviews.contribution: This project contributes an artist-led method in which live EEG features influence the birth, spread, connection, persistence, and decay of visual symbols. Its persistent visual memory allows earlier physiological changes to shape later forms, turning the artwork into an evolving process rather than a finished EEG image.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the proposed controlled comparison using the same EEG input for direct appearance mapping and for a rules-plus-memory system. Documenting both outputs over time can reveal what persistent memory contributes aesthetically and behaviourally.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is that the system has not yet been tested with live EEG, so its claims currently depend on simulated data. The project must address signal noise and artefacts, specify the feature-to-behaviour mapping, and demonstrate why EEG produces meaningful feedback beyond generic generative art.

reviews.project_title: Compendium Fireworks: An L-System Game-Journey Sculpture
reviews.contribution: This project contributes an annotated portfolio method that transforms an automatically recorded game journey—including movement paths, combat traces, and boss fireworks—into a physical sculpture. By comparing different playthroughs within the same L-system tree, it explores how players become creators of readable electronic artworks through play.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the working Godot prototype, which captures player actions and exports the L-system tree, route, and combat events as one three-dimensional form. Producing three annotated sculptures from different routes on a fixed tree would clearly connect individual choices to visible formal differences.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is preserving route and combat legibility while producing a structurally stable and printable sculpture. The project must also demonstrate that players experience authorship over the result, rather than receiving an automatically generated souvenir with little intentional control.

reviews.project_title: Provisional Title: The Continuous Body That Delay Takes Away
reviews.contribution: This project contributes an intermediate-level concept explaining how different photographic delays remove different aspects of continuous time. By pairing integration and sampling, it shows that one preserves continuity but loses bodily form, while the other preserves the body but deletes the intervals between moments.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest support is the paired production of two photographs from the same recorded duration and scene. This controlled comparison makes the temporal losses of exposure-based integration and computational sampling directly visible.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is proving that the perceived differences result from the two temporal methods rather than changes in framing, motion, lighting, or post-processing. The project should document identical capture conditions and test several scenes to demonstrate that the proposed concept extends beyond a single photographic pair.

reviews.project_title: Cross-Modal Generation of Embroidery Patterns from Traditional Music and Dynamic 3D Visualization
reviews.contribution: This project proposes an interpretable cross-modal framework that translates traditional musical structures into embroidery patterns, stitch paths, and dynamic 3D forms. Its main contribution is integrating music, pattern grammar, and fabrication constraints into one generative system.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence is the comparison of outputs produced from different musical genres and motif categories under the same generative rules. A physical embroidery sample could further demonstrate that the generated stitch paths are continuous and practically manufacturable.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is proving that the mappings between musical features and embroidery parameters are meaningful rather than arbitrary. The project should clearly define how melody, rhythm, and musical structure control specific visual and stitch parameters, and validate these relationships through controlled experiments.

reviews.project_title: A Photograph of Coexisting Memories: Through Narrative-Driven Computational Imaging
reviews.contribution: This project proposes a narrative-driven generative photography method that translates written recollections into traceable imaging parameters. By combining independent imaging states through spatial coexistence rules, it enables multiple, even contradictory, memories to remain visible within a single photograph.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence is a controlled comparison in which the same source photograph is processed through three predefined recollections and multiple coexistence rules. Parameter records, process diagrams, and visual comparisons can demonstrate that the final variations result from explicit computational rules rather than arbitrary editing.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is demonstrating that the final image is more than a conventional collage or local photo-editing effect. The project should clarify how narrative features control specific imaging parameters and explain why particular memory branches coexist according to particular spatial rules.

reviews.project_title: Generative Typography from Cantonese Street Names
reviews.contribution: This project proposes a generative typography method that translates the temporal features of Cantonese pronunciation into dynamic visual structures for Chinese characters and Roman letters. Its contribution lies in connecting phonetic structure, typographic generation, and the legibility requirements of public signage within one design framework.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence is a comparative set of outputs showing how the same phonetic rules control the structure, spacing, and movement of different Macau street names. Applying these rules consistently across Chinese and Roman writing systems, supported by parameter records and visual comparisons, would demonstrate the method’s traceability and transferability.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is establishing a meaningful and measurable relationship between Cantonese speech features and typographic parameters without unnecessarily reducing legibility. The project should define which phonetic features control which visual variables, identify the character structures that must remain unchanged, and verify the rules through controlled algorithmic comparisons.

reviews.project_title: Sonifying Bodily Movement for Embodied Reflection
reviews.contribution: This project proposes a non-evaluative movement-sonification framework that transforms upper-body motion into replayable sonic traces for embodied reflection and creative expression. Its contribution is to shift movement sonification away from classification, correction, and numerical scoring toward preserving rhythm, continuity, spatial relationships, and felt qualities.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence is a functioning interactive system that captures position, velocity, pauses, and left–right relationships and maps them into replayable sound. Comparative mapping experiments, replay records, and documented design iterations can demonstrate which movement qualities are preserved, transformed, or lost.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is ensuring that movement-to-sound mappings are understandable and experientially meaningful rather than arbitrary. The project should explain every mapping choice and demonstrate how replay enables reflection, while avoiding unsupported claims about therapeutic effects or improved bodily awareness.

reviews.project_title: From Unexpected Forms to Design Possibilities: Abductive Reasoning and Meaning Reconstruction in AI-Assisted Abstract 3D Form Ideation
reviews.contribution: This project proposes the intermediate concept of “deviation as signification” and develops a process model explaining how unexpected AI-generated forms become design resources through noticing, abductive reasoning, and meaning reconstruction. It also offers a preliminary typology of possible outcomes: new metaphors, new functions, new formal languages, or rejection.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence is a traceable first-person research record that documents the original intention, AI-generated deviation, immediate reaction, abductive guess, subsequent design decision, and discarded cases. Comparing multiple deviations through the same analytical loop can reveal recurring mechanisms rather than relying only on successful final objects.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is capturing fleeting subjective reactions without retrospectively overinterpreting them. The project should establish clear criteria for distinguishing a simple technical error from a meaningful design deviation and identify the precise point at which reinterpretation begins to influence the next design action.

reviews.project_title: When Two Signs Become One: Line-Width Thresholds in Cube-Edge Symbols
reviews.contribution: This project transforms the twelve edges of a cube into a constrained sign system and investigates the line-width threshold at which two structurally different signs become visually indistinguishable. Its contribution is to treat fabrication limits not merely as technical restrictions, but as conditions that determine whether a set of signs can continue to function as a distinguishable visual language.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence is the complete sequence of six physical prints, in which the selected cube edges remain unchanged and only line width increases systematically. Read as an annotated portfolio, the series can visibly identify the interval where separate edges merge and the two signs cease to remain distinct.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is defining a measurable criterion for when two signs have “become the same,” rather than relying only on personal visual judgement. Scale, printing device, material, resolution, and viewing distance should remain controlled so that the observed threshold can be attributed specifically to line width and fabrication conditions.

reviews.project_title: The Pond: Specimens of the Gaze
reviews.contribution: This project introduces the concepts of the “predatory gaze” and “peripheral coexistence,” reframing visual clarity as a form of taxidermy that turns living ambiguity into a fixed specimen. Its design contribution combines three gaze-driven states with cumulative gaze memory, making every act of possessive looking leave a lasting trace within the system.
reviews.strongest_support: The strongest evidence would be a functioning installation in which gaze direction, viewing distance, and duration visibly control calcification, collapse, and thawing in real time. System logs, an eight-hour time-lapse of accumulated shells, and short visitor interviews could demonstrate when viewers recognise that their own gaze is altering the habitat and whether they choose to step back.
reviews.main_challenge: The main challenge is ensuring that viewers understand the causal relationship between their gaze and the form’s “death,” rather than experiencing the transformation as an arbitrary visual effect. The gaze-duration threshold and peripheral-vision logic must therefore be carefully calibrated to avoid accidental activation, while the research should clearly state that it examines habits of possessive looking rather than actual biological life.
